editorial_reason: The source distinguishes R-linear maps of modules from the field-vector-space specialization. The general form needs additive homomorphism and compatibility with the same left R-scalar action on domain/codomain. Its vector version combines the two laws into one (the usual equivalence follows from T(0)=0). Field vector spaces are unital modules over K, but general R-modules need not be field vector spaces. The source also defines linear operator as a linear map from a module to itself; that is a specialization of domain/codomain, not a third inequivalent general definition. Be cautious that a noncommutative division-ring vector version requires compatible LEFT actions; our admitted field version explicitly restricts scalars to commutative K. No bijection, continuity, injectivity, surjectivity or finite-dimensionality is implied.

ProofWiki directly gives two equivalent formulations for the full set-theoretic image of a mapping: the set of codomain values with a preimage and the image f[S] of the whole domain. These formulations are mathematically identical for a total function, and constitute ONE meaning with two individually traced presentations. They are not the codomain T unless f is surjective, and not the image of an arbitrary subset A unless A=S. The source also presents a class-theoretic extension, which introduces different universe/class-mapping commitments; this broader version is not ingested automatically. The image of a K-linear transformation is a vector subspace, but that additional structure belongs to separately sourced results and is not assumed by this plain mapping definition.

The direct ProofWiki rank page explicitly assumes a linear transformation of vector spaces with FINITE-DIMENSIONAL image, then sets the rank equal to its dimension. This finite-image requirement is source-specific and must not be silently replaced by the unrestricted cardinal-valued dimension of an infinite-dimensional image or by the rank of an arbitrary module map. The mathematical image is the full mapping image T[V] from the independently sourced image of mapping, while field vector-space structure and K-linearity are independent prerequisites. The source references Warner, Nelson and its mathematical context, but those books were not independently read in this pass. The page is a redirect to ProofWiki's rank/linear-transformation article; retain the exact verified redirected source locator.

ProofWiki separately defines accumulation of a sequence using INFINITELY MANY indices in every neighborhood, and accumulation of a set by membership in the closure of A minus the queried point. They are not equivalent meanings: a constant sequence may accumulate at its repeated value although the singleton set has no set-accumulation point in a T1 space. Repeated indices matter, not distinct point values. The set formulation is valid in arbitrary topological spaces, with closure relative to X; the sequence formulation requires an indexed infinite sequence and does not imply convergence of its entire sequence. ProofWiki notes cluster point and limit point may use alternative conventions, so do not silently treat those names as identical in every source. Do not impose first countability or metric structure; only topological neighborhoods are used.
